reviewer: separate independent agent, same GPT family
method: Manual review of 19 pinned source README/license caches plus six supplemental license texts. No code executed, no service configured, no paid API called. Cached metadata may differ from text; text controls the recorded licensing scope.

findings.head: ba9b67df0f54ac78106ae85c552ef5d2458f7c9a
findings.license: Root LICENSE text is MIT; GitHub metadata is NOASSERTION. Dependency/plugin licenses are outside this check.
findings.facts: README documents a Linux workspace in Docker, desktop launchers including Windows, persistent storage, browser/desktop access, and optional host access. It still requires a model account/key or local inference.
findings.do_not_infer: A Docker workspace and launcher do not establish isolation from mounted host files, safe recursive delegation, or AWE recovery. Do not run the README installer commands as part of this audit.
findings.pilot: Disposable workspace; no host secrets; demonstrate recursive delegation limits, independent QA, abort propagation, deny host-file access, and recover a checkpoint after process termination.

findings.head: 67664e236ddcc45824b871d575677287599af152
findings.license: MIT text and metadata agree for the inspected repository.
findings.facts: README currently claims native Windows as well as Linux/macOS/WSL2, and local/Docker/SSH plus hosted terminal backends. Backend selection changes the execution boundary.
findings.do_not_infer: Do not preserve the outdated assumption that Hermes requires WSL. Do not infer all plugins/backends work on Windows. The README assertion that an antivirus alert is a false positive is not independent malware analysis; do not operationalize its antivirus exclusion instruction.
findings.pilot: Pin a release/artifact; verify provenance separately; exercise only a disposable terminal backend on the target OS, denied paths/network and a killed/resumed session. No blanket antivirus exclusions.

findings.head: 6ad8e7eb9d096aa3e2c7d291aa3d4cafa5f960ef
findings.license: Apache-2.0 outside ee directories; Enterprise License in ee areas, including auth, agent-builder and editor. Additional pinned LICENSE.md and ee/LICENSE inspected.
findings.facts: README offers agents/workflows, evals, observability and Node/React/Next integration. Those are source descriptions, not proof of the installed Head behavior.
findings.do_not_infer: Do not label all Mastra functionality Apache-2.0/free. Enterprise production needs both an appropriate written agreement and an enabling valid license key. Existing runtime identity must be established from owning code, not a product comparison.
findings.pilot: Map the exact packages/features to licenses. Use a copy of the present Head to compare bounded recursion, cancellation, session recovery and QA separation before considering any replacement.

supplemental_license_refs.summary: Mastra core uses Apache-2.0 outside ee directories. The mapping explicitly names core auth, agent-builder, and editor EE areas.
supplemental_license_refs.inspection_scope: LICENSE text only; no legal clearance or feature entitlement assumed

supplemental_license_refs.summary: Enterprise code is source available. Production use requires both a written agreement permitting the relevant feature and a valid feature-enabling license key; development/testing is separately defined. Production, redistribution and evaluation must not be treated as interchangeable.
supplemental_license_refs.inspection_scope: LICENSE text only; no legal clearance or feature entitlement assumed

findings.head: 52d1c4cd80162fbf03d7f92def0cb1631f1edfd4
findings.license: MIT outside litellm/enterprise; that subtree has commercial terms. Root reference without extension returns 404; actual pinned license is LICENSE.md.
findings.facts: README documents a gateway/SDK, routing, spend tracking, virtual keys and provider integrations. Some authentication/administration functions are enterprise features.
findings.do_not_infer: The gateway is not a token seller or a guarantee of provider availability, payment support, cost accuracy or hard spending limits. Readme production-ready and benchmark claims are unproven for AWE.
findings.pilot: Without paid inference, use a controlled mock upstream to test timeout/retry budgets, duplicate effects, model/tool capability filters, auth and stop-on-budget. Later real inference needs its own cost authorization.

supplemental_license_refs.summary: Enterprise-directory production use requires an applicable agreement and valid enterprise license for the correct seats. Development/testing permissions do not grant unrestricted redistribution or production rights.
supplemental_license_refs.inspection_scope: LICENSE text only; no legal clearance or feature entitlement assumed

findings.head: 5a5894a77604e3148b0f76b14d8b0d9e4411edcb
findings.license: MIT text and metadata agree for this source repository.
findings.facts: README documents eligible provider routing, free-tier pools, opt-in masking, TLS/proxy/MITM features, and exclusions for providers marked avoid.
findings.do_not_infer: Free-tier headlines and savings are vendor claims; they do not prove usable models, account eligibility, legal/provider permission, recurring quota, RF payment access, or quality. Do not activate trust-store/MITM installation or reuse broad OAuth/subscription tokens.
findings.pilot: Read-only configuration review first; then mock capability/failover/budget tests with one explicit allowed provider. Prove no unapproved credential forwarding, retries or route to avoid-marked providers.

findings.head: ac4a1326dc0ab75a43c7ccd2d3932965eab24201
findings.license: Apache-2.0 text and metadata agree for ToolHive itself; managed servers retain their own licenses.
findings.facts: README documents Docker/Podman/Kubernetes runtime, MCP gateway/registry, and identity/access policy when configured with an authentication source.
findings.do_not_infer: Containerization is not an independent code-safety audit. Do not claim per-request identity enforcement without configuring and testing its auth source. A curated registry entry is not APPROVED for AWE.
findings.pilot: Use a harmless test MCP with minimum mounts/caps and no credentials; prove deny filesystem/network/unauthenticated call, per-user access, complete audit evidence and termination.

findings.head: 488c30d9d16e4993bc548ad298eb7450f5125c93
findings.license: License is transitioning MIT to Apache-2.0, with retained MIT contributions and CC-BY-4.0 documentation; NOASSERTION is expected for this mixed text.
findings.facts: Inspector is a connect/list/call/debug tool. README says default secret storage uses OS keychain if available, otherwise a file that is unencrypted without a supplied key.
findings.do_not_infer: Inspector is not a sandbox, independent QA decision maker, or screenshot-diff tool. Do not assume a headless/container machine has an encrypted keychain-backed store.
findings.pilot: Inspect storage selection on the target environment using fake tokens. Verify memory-only/encrypted mode, no secret leakage into logs/exports, and negative MCP response handling.

findings.head: e1dc4b18dbb948921da37f3d4224a628730b43b0
findings.license: Same MIT-to-Apache-2.0 transition; documentation license is distinct.
findings.facts: Root README explicitly presents these as educational reference MCP implementations and asks users to evaluate their own security safeguards.
findings.do_not_infer: Official repository ownership does not make these production-ready servers or a collective audit of every third-party server. Archived servers may have newer owners/replacements.
findings.pilot: Choose one exact server and version; test allowed directories or database scopes, traversal/symlink/URI attacks, auth, cancellation and audit logs. Do not deploy the complete examples collection.

findings.head: 78eca85361efb545a4c0f59b6140aef0721c5412
findings.license: Apache-2.0 text and metadata agree for the inspected MCP server.
findings.facts: README requires Node >=18, defaults to persistent browser profiles, documents isolated sessions, and explicitly says origin controls and Playwright MCP are not security boundaries.
findings.do_not_infer: Do not grant a personal browser profile to an agent or equate origin allowlists with egress isolation. Redirects and local file access require independent controls; several example modes disable browser sandboxing.
findings.pilot: Dedicated profile or isolated context, separate per concurrent agent. Test redirected egress, local-file denial, cookie separation, sensitive URL redaction, download handling and explicit approval for account-changing actions.

findings.head: 6fbcd00b2034502ba3001a49dfaf93593aee7069
findings.license: MIT text/metadata in the inspected cache; API usage and account permissions remain separate.
findings.facts: README documents OAuth/PAT login, toolsets and exact tools, read-only filtering, and many tools with write/admin scopes. Read-only filtering takes priority in documented configuration.
findings.do_not_infer: An MCP connection is not blanket owner permission. A repository-readable token does not justify admin, workflow, deletion or write actions. Hosted and local implementations have different auth behavior.
findings.pilot: Start with a selected disposable repository and read-only tool allowlist plus minimal token scopes. Verify denied writes, repo boundaries, duplicate mutations/leases, secret redaction and approval semantics before any writes.

findings.head: cd3697e07eb520056dcf142d0c7439bbb9ba32e9
findings.facts: Despite the googleworkspace organization name, README states this is not an officially supported Google product. It requires a GCP OAuth project/credentials or a supplied token and warns about oversized scope presets in testing-mode apps.
findings.do_not_infer: Do not promise official support, unrestricted free quotas, existing account consent, or send/write authorization. Local token encryption does not mean the agent cannot use the token with its granted powers.
findings.pilot: Separate test account/project; select only required read scopes and services. Prove tool discovery, token isolation, revocation and that mail/calendar/Drive writes stay denied until explicitly authorized.

findings.head: 65286d80c77589fbe43c85b870979d67794cc91c
findings.license: MIT source text observed; README dependency-wide license statements have not been independently audited.
findings.facts: Community Workspace MCP documents OAuth, read-only mode, service/tool filters, per-service permissions, multi-user HTTP modes and optional tracing.
findings.do_not_infer: Claims of secure organization hosting, no telemetry and permissive dependency licensing are source assertions. Do not infer tested tenant isolation or least privilege from OAuth 2.1 naming alone. Insecure-transport snippets are local examples.
findings.pilot: Two test users with disjoint fake data; narrow scopes/tools and read-only mode. Prove cross-user denial, correct bearer-token validation, secret storage, tool-union behavior and absence of trace-content leakage.

findings.head: ddd90f3a6d454ea0b2fc29f1b084f50fd062b880
findings.license: MIT source text observed; API redirect resolves the original sonnylazuardi URL to grab/cursor-talk-to-figma-mcp.
findings.facts: Community bridge uses a Figma plugin and socket connection. README Windows/WSL instructions include binding 0.0.0.0.
findings.do_not_infer: Do not present this as the official Figma service or assume the socket is authenticated because it is local. Binding all interfaces can expose design-write capability. Successful node edits do not establish visual fidelity or design-system compliance.
findings.pilot: Disposable Figma document and explicit connection scope; verify origin/channel/auth handling, no other documents accessible, rollback, text fidelity and independent visual QA. Keep the socket loopback-only unless an isolated network design is tested.

findings.head: 4f4ab8973b76e474770a57d544c2fdc967d0e0e2
findings.license: Community content is MIT; packages/ee and server API ee areas have commercial terms. Pinned enterprise terms inspected.
findings.facts: README describes integrations and a no-code/workflow builder, including enterprise capabilities.
findings.do_not_infer: Do not treat advertised enterprise RBAC/security functions as available under core MIT, or a workflow builder as proof of dynamic recursive agent orchestration. Workflows can execute account mutations through stored credentials.
findings.pilot: One deterministic adapter flow with a fake credential, explicit read-only action, error/timeout/retry tests and idempotency. Map every selected piece/dependency and enterprise feature before reuse.

supplemental_license_refs.summary: Enterprise production use requires applicable subscription terms or another governing agreement and a valid enterprise license for the correct seats. Core MIT terms do not cover these directories.
supplemental_license_refs.inspection_scope: LICENSE text only; no legal clearance or feature entitlement assumed

findings.head: 1ae5175a008fc464cc27579b4d7613b60e203ed1
findings.license: Sustainable Use License for covered main-branch content, with separate Enterprise exceptions. The text limits use/distribution; it is not an unrestricted MIT/Apache grant.
findings.facts: README offers visual workflows, code, approvals and self-hosted/cloud modes; root license has file/directory and branch restrictions.
findings.do_not_infer: Do not call the entire product unrestricted open source or assume commercial redistribution/hosted resale is allowed. Internal/personal usage and SaaS redistribution require different scope decisions.
findings.pilot: Choose exact permitted deployment/use case first. Use a disposable workflow to prove credential scoping, cancellation, retries/idempotency, export/recovery and no unsanctioned account actions.

findings.head: 9621bc46d0e67e7580f6425dea07996f347f0412
findings.license: MIT outside listed EE directories; enterprise periphery has separate commercial terms.
findings.facts: README documents OpenTelemetry-based traces, evals, prompts, costs and self-hosted/cloud deployments.
findings.do_not_infer: Observability is not an independent QA verdict. Do not infer that traces are secret-free or that self-hosting automatically satisfies retention, tenant isolation or cost accuracy. README scale claims are not AWE load tests.
findings.pilot: Synthetic traces containing canary secrets; prove redaction before storage/export, retention/deletion and access boundaries. Check instrumented tool actions and missing-event detection independently of the system under review.

supplemental_license_refs.summary: The enterprise periphery has commercial terms, while root-defined core remains MIT. Enterprise use depends on the governing agreement and valid license; development/testing copying and modification are separately allowed.
supplemental_license_refs.inspection_scope: LICENSE text only; no legal clearance or feature entitlement assumed

findings.head: 4dcb599d9455c117e7de0ac176744eb20cc37f0e
findings.license: MIT outside any EE directory; backend/src/ee/LICENSE.md specifies commercial production conditions. Not every advertised access feature is covered by core MIT.
findings.facts: README describes secrets, certificates, privileged access and agent access; Docker setup includes Windows instructions.
findings.do_not_infer: A vault product does not make end-to-end secret handling safe: agents/tools can still exfiltrate grants, environment values or output. Do not infer free entitlements for advertised approvals/enterprise policy functions.
findings.pilot: Fake secret with narrow machine identity and time-limited access; prove denial outside scope, rotation/revocation and no leak to subprocess output, model context, logs or checkpoint exports. Test backup/restore on disposable data.

supplemental_license_refs.summary: The discovered backend EE license requires an agreement and valid enterprise license for production use. Root MIT applies outside EE exclusions; not every advertised secret-management feature is thereby established as free.
supplemental_license_refs.inspection_scope: LICENSE text only; no legal clearance or feature entitlement assumed

findings.head: dc4c26eaf06131c74c1067ec62e309d11f77040d
findings.license: Apache-2.0 text observed; repository has moved from alibaba/OpenSandbox to opensandbox-group/OpenSandbox.
findings.facts: README documents Docker/Kubernetes sandboxes, code/command/file/browser access, optional Firecracker runtime and egress/vault features. It explicitly records a signing/provenance gap for current umbrella releases.
findings.do_not_infer: Do not state all release images are signed or all backends offer the same security boundary. A sandbox API with commands is a privileged execution service; defaults, mounts, egress and control-plane access need tests.
findings.pilot: Pin image digest; establish available signing evidence for that release. Validate no host mounts/privileged socket access, egress deny, command quota/timeouts, cancellation, checkpoint isolation and secret brokerage with a disposable payload.

findings.head: 5b40cc2da4c2bf10f6b6b00204141eab274c4255
findings.license: Root MIT source text observed for the inspected repository; cloud service and separate backends have their own terms.
findings.facts: Current README describes local execution by default, optional Docker sandboxes and multiple conversation sandboxes. It says conversation isolation does not sandbox the whole Canvas/automation service and shared host workspaces remain shared.
findings.do_not_infer: Do not reuse older product descriptions or claim all execution is containerized. A multi-agent UI does not establish mission-bounded recursion or conflict-free parallel work. Docker/local network-auth examples are conditional.
findings.pilot: Separate worktrees per agent; minimal container mounts; prove shared-directory conflicts are prevented, host/service boundary, strong session auth, approval for mutations and recovery of both conversation state and source tree.

critical_do_not_infer: README description or GitHub metadata is not sandbox/security/production certification.
A permissive root license does not cover excluded enterprise directories, hosted terms, dependencies or model/provider access.
MCP is a protocol; source descriptions do not grant execution or write authorization.
Model routing software is not inference credit, payment eligibility, quality assurance or a verified hard budget.
An independent agent in the same GPT family does not satisfy the requested different-family gate.
